Status

Current State

June 24 documentation records pfSense forwarding selected system, firewall, authentication, VPN, and gateway events to Linux01 at 10.10.30.20:514, with Linux01 rsyslog listeners and alert-match logging. Current Proxmox metadata validates Linux01 is running on VLAN 30 and QEMU guest agent is responding.

Evidence

  • Proxmox current API: Linux01 VM 400 running, tag=30, guest agent responding.
  • DNS current command: linux01.ad.jeremyfontenot.online resolves to 10.10.30.20.
  • June 24 IP-address-documented documentation: pfSense-to-Linux01 rsyslog forwarding and alert logging documented.
  • Current reachability check: TCP 514 from the current client path timed out and is not treated as rsyslog service failure.
  • inventories/linux01-inventory-20260626-020257.json: SSH from the management execution path timed out; guest-side rsyslog state was NOT TESTED.
  • inventories/linux01-inventory-20260626-084312.json: authenticated target-local Linux01 inventory validates rsyslog service/listener state, route/DNS state, AD integration indicators, disk capacity, and logrotate summary.
  • evidence/linux01-local-inventory-validation-20260626-035220.md: sanitized evidence for Linux01 target-local inventory import and validation.

Target State

Expand centralized logging beyond pfSense by adding documented, least-privilege log forwarding or collection for Windows and Proxmox sources without weakening existing firewall policy.

Candidate target design, pending implementation approval:

  • Keep Linux01 as the primary syslog receiver because target-local evidence now confirms available root filesystem capacity, active rsyslog listeners on 10.10.30.20:514 for TCP and UDP, and rsyslog log rotation. UFW source restrictions still require a clearer privileged summary before any new source is added.
  • Evaluate Windows Event Forwarding for DC01 and WS01 with DC01 as the likely Windows Event Collector only if existing domain policy and firewall posture support it safely. Do not make DC01 a collector until a separate change plan covers subscription type, source computers, event channels, retention, and rollback.
  • Evaluate Proxmox remote syslog forwarding to Linux01 or another approved receiver only after documenting source IP, destination IP, protocol, port, and retention.
  • Keep Linux local logs on Linux01 in local journald/rsyslog paths unless an approved monitoring platform is introduced.

Exact Systems

  • Linux01 VM 400
  • DC01 VM 200
  • WS01 VM 300
  • Proxmox host 192.168.0.242
  • pfSense VM 100

Exact Commands

Discovery and planning only until approved:

pwsh -NoProfile -File .\scripts\linux\Get-LinuxReadOnlyInventory.ps1
pwsh -NoProfile -File .\scripts\active-directory\Invoke-DC01LocalReadOnlyCollection.ps1
pwsh -NoProfile -File .\scripts\windows-server\Invoke-WS01LocalReadOnlyCollection.ps1

Implementation commands are intentionally not authorized in this change plan. Linux01 rsyslog state has been validated, but Windows Event Forwarding, Proxmox logging state, pfSense sender configuration, and any firewall or GPO requirements still need a dedicated approved implementation plan.

Target-local validation commands prepared for the next inventory pass:

run_id="$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
bash ./Invoke-Linux01LocalReadOnlyCollection.sh "/tmp/linux01-inventory-${run_id}.json"

Required Privileges

  • Read-only collection: existing approved sessions.
  • Any logging configuration change: administrative privileges on the target system and explicit approval.

Network Requirements

No firewall openings are approved by this plan. Any proposed log path must identify source, destination, protocol, port, and existing firewall state before implementation.

Expected network review before implementation:

  • pfSense to Linux01 syslog path: verify existing source restriction, protocol, and port from configuration evidence before changing anything.
  • DC01 and WS01 to collector: identify whether Windows Event Forwarding uses existing domain/Kerberos paths or requires new firewall scope. Any firewall or GPO change requires a dedicated approved plan.
  • Proxmox to Linux01 syslog: document management-network source, Linux VLAN destination, routing path, and firewall requirements before implementation.

Security Impact

Positive if implemented carefully: stronger audit trail and troubleshooting visibility. Risk if overbroad: excessive log exposure, sensitive log retention, or unnecessary inter-network access.

Security controls required in the implementation plan:

  • Exclude credentials, private keys, Kerberos tickets, certificate private material, and sensitive raw log excerpts from repository evidence.
  • Prefer source-restricted firewall rules over broad subnet acceptance if any new rules are approved.
  • Document whether logs are unauthenticated syslog, authenticated Windows Event Forwarding, or locally collected files.
  • Define integrity expectations honestly; plain syslog improves visibility but does not provide strong transport integrity by itself.

Service-Impact Risk

Low for discovery. Medium for configuration changes because logging service reloads or firewall changes could disrupt visibility or access if done incorrectly.

Implementation must avoid service restarts unless the approved plan explicitly requires them. Prefer configuration validation and reload-only workflows where technically appropriate.

Retention, Rotation, and Capacity

Linux01 authenticated inventory currently supports:

  • Root filesystem capacity: 19 GiB total, 13 GiB available, 29 percent used.
  • Current rsyslog listener state: TCP and UDP 514 listening on 10.10.30.20.
  • Current rsyslog destination templates/configuration: /var/log/remote/%FROMHOST-IP%/messages.log and /var/log/remote/pfsense-alerts.log are configured.
  • Current logrotate policy for rsyslog-managed files: weekly rotation, four rotations, compression, missing files tolerated, empty files skipped.
  • Disk-use alert threshold. Initial planning threshold: warning at 80 percent used, critical at 90 percent used, pending Jeremy approval.
  • Failure behavior if Linux01 is unavailable: sources should continue local logging and must not block authentication, DNS, DHCP, routing, or VM operation.

Alerting

Alerting remains planned. Candidate non-invasive alerts after receiver validation:

  • Linux01 log filesystem above threshold.
  • rsyslog service inactive.
  • No pfSense log receipt within an expected interval.
  • Proxmox backup job failure or missing latest backup.
  • Windows Event Forwarding subscription source inactive, if WEF is later approved.

Validation

  • Confirm log sender service state.
  • Confirm listener state on Linux01.
  • Send one controlled non-sensitive test event.
  • Confirm event arrives in the expected file or index.
  • Confirm no credentials or private data are written to repository evidence.

Rollback

  • Revert only the logging configuration added by the approved implementation.
  • Restore any exported pre-change configuration where applicable.
  • Restart/reload only affected logging services if required and approved.

Evidence Capture

  • Timestamped pre-change inventory.
  • Sanitized configuration diff or export.
  • Exact command transcript with secrets omitted.
  • Controlled test-event result.
  • Rollback verification.

Approval Requirement

Explicit Jeremy approval is required before any logging configuration, firewall, service, package, or scheduled-task change.

Claim Boundary

This plan is implementation-ready documentation only. It does not implement centralized logging expansion, change firewall policy, install software, restart services, or modify any infrastructure system. Linux01 rsyslog receiver state is now validated by target-local inventory; additional sources and alerting remain planned until separately approved and implemented.

Recovered VMM host-agent health

HVHOST01 initially reported Needs Attention with VMM error 12704 even though vmms and SCVMMAgent were running and both server and agent were version 10.22.1287.0. WinRM tests passed. A VMM Run As account named HVHOST01 Management was created with the validated domain-management credential and assigned under Host Access. After refresh, host status, network, WinRM, agent service, and agent version all reported OK.

10

Modeled the isolated AD network

Validated the VMM logical network ad and network site AD-10.10.20.0-24 for subnet 10.10.20.0/24. The static VMM IP pool spans 10.10.20.201 through 10.10.20.220 and VMM reports the logical network as Fully compliant.

11

Resolved logical-switch conversion blockers

The existing External-LAN standard switch could not convert while the VMM logical switch used a different minimum-bandwidth mode and uplink teaming mode. The Host management port profile weight was cleared, HomeLab-Logical-Switch was changed to Absolute bandwidth mode, and its uplink mode was changed to No Uplink Team to match the single-adapter standard switch.

12

Converted to a VMM logical switch

Converted External-LAN into HomeLab-Logical-Switch using the HomeLab-Uplink uplink profile. VMM completed the host-change job successfully, Hyper-V reported the new external switch name, and the host management vNIC retained 10.10.20.102/24, gateway 10.10.20.1, and DNS 10.10.20.10.

13

Applied a VM traffic classification

Adjusted the built-in Medium Bandwidth Adapter profile so it was compatible with the logical switch's Absolute bandwidth mode, mapped the Medium bandwidth classification into HomeLab-Logical-Switch, and assigned that classification to APP01's virtual network adapter.

14

Validated guest network and domain services

APP01 remained connected to HomeLab-Logical-Switch with status Ok. Inside the guest, 10.10.20.103/24, gateway 10.10.20.1, and DNS 10.10.20.10 remained intact. Gateway ping succeeded, DC01 resolved to 10.10.20.10, and TCP 389 to the domain controller succeeded.

15

Exercised checkpoint lifecycle

Created the VMM checkpoint Pre-VMM-Lab-Changes while APP01 remained running, verified the checkpoint in APP01 properties, then deleted it and confirmed the checkpoint list returned to empty.

16

Protected resource headroom

Measured HVHOST01 at four logical processors and about 8 GB RAM. APP01 Dynamic Memory was already configured with 2048 MB minimum, 4096 MB startup, and 6144 MB maximum; its active assignment had settled to 2 GB with memory status OK. No additional Windows VM was deployed so the nested host retained practical headroom.

Observed results

The management behaviors were exercised, not inferred.

Host health

HVHOST01 status OK

Network, WinRM, Host Agent Service, Host Agent Version, and overall host health were returned to OK after assigning the Run As account.

Logical network

10.10.20.0/24 fully compliant

The ad logical network, network site, and 20-address VMM pool were recognized as fully compliant.

Logical switch

External-LAN converted successfully

HVHOST01 now exposes HomeLab-Logical-Switch as the external Hyper-V switch while preserving the existing host management IP path.

VM networking

APP01 classification and connectivity

APP01 uses HomeLab-Logical-Switch with the Medium bandwidth classification and retained working gateway, DNS, and LDAP connectivity.

Lifecycle

Checkpoint create and delete

The VMM checkpoint workflow completed without stopping APP01, and cleanup returned the VM to a checkpoint-free state.

Scoped remote access

OpenVPN management retained

Remote administration continued through the lab VPN path rather than exposing the isolated 10.10.20.0/24 network directly to the home subnet.

Screenshot evidence

Preserved VMM screenshots anchor the management story.

The gallery contains the previously imported SCVMM working-session screenshots. The August 15 update extends the same case study with the validated logical-network, logical-switch, host-health, APP01 classification, connectivity, and checkpoint work recorded during the VMM project session.

Inspect screenshot hashes and provenanceTrace the public claim

Scope and limitations

A working management lab, not an enterprise VMM deployment.

The evidence supports a single SCVMM 2022 management server, one managed nested Hyper-V host, one observed guest, a VMM logical network and IP pool, conversion of an existing external switch into a VMM logical switch, VM port classification, remote lifecycle control, checkpoint handling, VM Viewer access, and a scoped OpenVPN management path. It does not prove clustering, high availability, live migration, Storage Spaces Direct, enterprise scale, production availability, security assurance, or management of Proxmox guests through VMM.

The project extends an existing on-premises Windows management path into Azure without moving the workloads out of the lab. Problem, objective, and architecture

Add cloud-based inventory and extension management while keeping the lab on premises.

The objective was to represent two Windows Server systems and the VMM01 SQL instance in Azure, preserve the existing local management design, and make every public claim traceable to current evidence.

Role of Proxmox

Proxmox supplies the QEMU virtualization layer. Both Arc-enabled Windows servers remain running as personal-lab virtual machines; Azure Arc does not replace or directly manage the hypervisor.

Role of Windows Admin Center

Windows Admin Center provides the local connection inventory and Azure integration surface. Its connection list shows both HVHOST01 and VMM01 with Azure Arc status Connected.

Identity separation

The Windows Admin Center gateway uses an on-premises Windows identity, while Azure integration uses a separate Azure identity. Public screenshots redact both account names and the email address while preserving the visible signed-in states.

Resource-group and RBAC boundary

The collected resources are grouped under rg-hybrid-lab-centralus-01. The current evidence does not enumerate role assignments, so it supports resource-group scope but makes no claim about a specific Owner, Contributor, or custom Azure RBAC role.

Onboarding and troubleshooting

Validate the missing agent, use the generated script, and verify the resulting Azure resource.

1. Connectivity before installation

The Windows Admin Center workflow initially appeared to stall while installing the Arc agent. Direct validation found that the Connected Machine agent executable was absent, while outbound TCP 443 connectivity to gbl.his.arc.azure.com succeeded.

2. Manual onboarding script

The Azure-generated onboarding script was transferred to VMM01 and executed through the authorized PowerShell remoting path. The agent installed, authenticated, created the Azure resource, and reported Connected.

3. Agent and service validation

Fresh direct validation on HVHOST01 confirmed agent version 1.67.03504.3207, Connected status, enabled agent auto-upgrade, successful TCP 443 reachability, and the himds, ExtensionService, and GCArcService services running with Automatic startup.

4. Current access limitation

VMM01 answered WinRM but rejected the current Windows credential for a fresh remote session. Its local Arc and SQL services were not re-read directly during this collection; Azure portal and Windows Admin Center supplied the current connected, extension, SQL inventory, licensing, and telemetry evidence.

SQL Server discovery and extension

Move from a pending extension to a connected SQL inventory record.

Initial extension state

The SQL extension initially remained in Creating/ENABLING while the SqlServerExtension service was StartPending. Onboarding logs showed least-privilege configuration and local-group membership work still in progress.

Observed resolution

The service later reached Running, the WindowsAgent.SqlServer extension reached Succeeded, SQL inventory appeared, and DPS upload status reached OK. The current portal evidence shows extension version 1.1.3518.465 with automatic upgrade enabled.

Licensing decision

The Arc-enabled SQL resource reports SQL Server 2022 Developer edition. License only is selected instead of pay-as-you-go; Developer edition is not presented as production licensed.

Services not inferred

Azure Monitor, Azure Backup, Update Manager, Defender, Site Recovery, automated SQL updates, and automatic SQL backups are not described as enabled. The SQL overview explicitly showed automated updates and automatic backups Disabled.

Verified final state

Current results are separated from historical troubleshooting.

Connected

HVHOST01 Arc machine

Azure portal and direct agent output both report Connected in Central US; the three Arc services were running and TCP 443 validation succeeded.

Connected

VMM01 Arc machine

Succeeded

WindowsAgent.SqlServer

Version 1.1.3518.465 reports Succeeded, no update available, and automatic upgrade Enabled.

Connected · telemetry OK

VMM01 SQL Server instance

SQL Server 2022 Developer is inventoried in connected mode with License only, DPS OK, metrics OK, and Connected Machine agent status Connected.

Security and privacy controls

Publish the evidence, not the identities or control-plane identifiers.

Private originals

Fresh raw captures were retained outside the public repository. Published PNG files are cropped derivatives with tenant IDs, subscription IDs, account names, email addresses, private IP addresses, and unnecessary interface data removed or redacted.

No authentication material

No passwords, MFA codes, device-login codes, tokens, cookies, private keys, connection strings, or raw authentication logs are published.

Integrity records

The evidence manifest records SHA-256 hashes, byte sizes, dimensions, source context, transformation notes, and the specific claim supported by every public screenshot.

Least-claim posture

Connected and Succeeded states are reported only where current evidence shows them. Unavailable direct VMM01 service validation remains a named limitation.

Screenshot evidence

Fresh views from PowerShell, Proxmox, Windows Admin Center, and Azure.

Each image is a cropped and redacted derivative of a newly captured authenticated view. Captions state exactly what the visible fields support.

Limitations and next steps

A verified hybrid-management lab, not a production Azure operations claim.

The evidence supports two Arc-connected Windows Server lab machines, one Arc-enabled SQL Server 2022 Developer instance, current extension and telemetry states, and direct HVHOST01 agent/service validation. It does not prove production administration, enterprise scale, broad Azure RBAC ownership, high availability, disaster recovery, SLA performance, security assurance, or enabled Azure services beyond the fields shown. VMM01 local service state was not freshly read because the current Windows credential was rejected.

Practical next steps are to restore an approved VMM01 remoting path, repeat the local service and SQL checks, document the exact Azure RBAC assignment through a public-safe export, and evaluate optional Azure services separately before making any enablement claim.
